definition.simple: Anything that has weight and takes up space. Like your book, water, or even the air in a balloon!
definition.academic: Matter is defined as anything that has mass and occupies volume (space).

common_misconceptions: Thoughts, emotions (like love or anger), and energy (like heat or light) are NOT matter because they don't have mass or take up space.
ai_context.tutor_hint: Ask the student to name 3 things in their room that are matter, and 1 thing that is NOT matter.

definition.simple: When things mix together on their own. Like when the smell of good food spreads from the kitchen to your room.
definition.academic: The intermixing of particles of two different types of matter on their own by finding space between each other.

examples: Ink dropping into a glass of water and turning it blue

common_misconceptions: Diffusion only happens in gases. False! It happens in liquids too (like ink in water), and very slowly in solids.
ai_context.tutor_hint: Remind students that heating increases the rate of diffusion because particles move faster.

definition.simple: When a solid turns directly into a gas without becoming a liquid first. It just skips a step!
definition.academic: The change of state directly from solid to gas on heating and vice versa on cooling, without passing through the liquid state.

examples: Dry ice (solid CO2) turning to fog

common_misconceptions: All solids melt into liquids before turning into gas. False! Sublimable solids skip the liquid phase completely.
ai_context.tutor_hint: Ask if they have ever seen naphthalene balls (used to keep insects away in clothes) slowly disappear over months.

definition.simple: The 'hidden' heat. When you melt ice, it stays at 0°C even if you keep heating it, until all the ice is melted. The heat goes into breaking the bonds, not raising the temperature.
definition.academic: The heat energy required to change the state of a substance without changing its temperature.

common_misconceptions: Heating a substance always increases its temperature. False! During a change of state (melting/boiling), temperature stays constant because the heat is used to break intermolecular forces.
ai_context.tutor_hint: The word 'latent' literally means 'hidden' in Latin.
